title: Unique permutation with maximal stabilization
source: Connor Ahlbach, “Tableau Stabilization and Rectangular Tableaux Fixed by Promotion Powers”, arXiv:1907.00105 (2019). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00105)

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-343104-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-343104.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; BRIDGE: published lemma, exact; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For every n >= 1 and every permutation w of size n, the stabilization index of w equals n if and only if w is the identity: the increasing permutation stabilizes at n, and every permutation with a descent stabilizes by n-1. This proves Ahlbach's conjecture that the increasing permutation is the unique permutation with maximal stabilization. Lean defines stabilization through the row-insertion tableau of the k-fold reading word and checks that every entry of the last copy stays in its original row; the identification of this with the source's definition by jeu de taquin rectification is the source's Lemma 2.10 (a classical theorem of Schutzenberger, cited from Fulton), which is not checked in Lean. The hypothesis n >= 1 is needed and matches the source.
significance.caveat: The kernel-checked definition of stabilization is the row-insertion form; the bridge to the source's rectification form is the classical identity Rect(S) = P(reading word of S) (source Lemma 2.10, from Fulton), trusted and not formalized. An independent referee computed stabilization both ways for all 46,233 permutations with n <= 8 and found agreement, and agreement with Ahlbach's published distribution. Bounded literature search; two citation indexes refused requests.

root_basis: Root extracted the fifteen modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee checked every convention of the Lean definition against the source, wrote its own jeu de taquin rectification and compared it with a transcription of the Lean definition on all permutations with n <= 8, read the paper line by line and supplied the revised paper used here. Root accepts the row-insertion endpoint with the classical bridge lemma stated as a caveat.
